# Session notes — Cart bundle (SFCC-11), pre-build decisions

> **BUILD HANDOFF: start at `~/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-11/HANDOFF.md`.**
> Planning is CLOSED. Gate is clean, no blockers. Single PR, 18 commits, branch
> `feature/SFCC-11_cart` off `develop` @ `71025f18`. This file is the decision record and the full
> Figma spec; `plan.md` is the executable plan; `findings.md` is the gate.


**Written:** 2026-09-16
**Branch at time of writing:** `feature/SFCC-831-689_country-language-mismatch` (NOT the build branch — a
fresh `feature/*` off `develop` is needed before any cart work starts)
**Scope:** card-by-card requirements pass over 7 Cart stories, ahead of a bundled build.
**Status:** all 7 cards read, all ACs pulled and adjudicated. No code written. No Jira updated.

The ACs do **not** live in the Jira description — they are in custom field `customfield_10231`
("Acceptance Criteria", project-scoped, textarea). Fetching only the description misses them
entirely. Some return plain text, some return ADF (`{type: "doc"}`) — SFCC-315/270/795 came back
as ADF and needed flattening.

---

## 1. The bundle

All 7 are Epic SFCC-11 (Cart), SFCC Sprint 5 (active, 2026-09-07 → 2026-09-21), label `Squad-A`,
assigned to Marcel, status **Ready for Development**.

| Card | Title | Priority | Reqs |
|---|---|---|---|
| SFCC-315 | Drawer Component (Cart Variation) – PWA Kit Component | High | CAI-006 |
| SFCC-270 | Cart Item Component UI (Part 1) – PWA Kit Component | High | CAI-006 |
| SFCC-795 | Cart Item Component UI (Part 2) – PWA Kit Component | Medium | — |
| SFCC-271 | Cart Item Component – Quantity Stepper | High | CAI-007 |
| SFCC-272 | Cart Item – Remove and Wishlist Actions | High | CAI-008, CAI-018 |
| SFCC-250 | Cart – Maximum Purchase Quantity Enforcement per SKU | Medium | CAI-017, PRD-011 |
| SFCC-275 | Cart Page – Button Group | High | CAI-010 |

### Bundle-shape decision

One gather pass and one plan across all 7 (done — this document). **Not** one mega-PR.
Rationale: a single PR converts 7 independently-mergeable units into one all-or-nothing unit;
one change-requested story would block the other six. Cart also spans two squads' Tier 2
ownership (`order-summary`/`promo-code` = Squad A, `product-item` = Squad B), so a single PR pulls
in both code-owner reviews at once, and AGENTS.md Hard Rule #10 requires explicit scope
confirmation before touching more than one protection tier in one change.

**Exception:** SFCC-250 and SFCC-272 are welded at the cart's `onAuthSuccess` seam (see §5) and
build as one PR. Accepted deliberately.

### A real CI consequence, not yet addressed

`qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` job has no **`cart`** e2e area. The existing areas are `homepage`,
`checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`. `e2e-localhost` only runs when every
e2e-relevant changed file falls inside exactly one area's allow-list — otherwise it resolves to
`e2e_scope: skip` and **does not run at all** on that PR. So every cart PR currently gets no
PR-time E2E. Adding a `cart` allow-list group + `@cart` tags is a deliberate step in the plan, not
something to discover afterwards. See `.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E.

---

## 2. Verified findings (evidence-backed — re-verify before relying on any of these)

### 2.1 SFCC has no max-order-quantity field. The frontend constant IS the implementation.

- `commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts` contains `minOrderQuantity` (6 occurrences) and
  `stepQuantity`. **No `maxOrderQuantity` anywhere.**
- Live probe against the dev sandbox (site `ZimmermannAU`, shortCode `qmyt7hks`, SLAS private-client
  `client_credentials` guest token, mirroring `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `liveCheckSfcc`), two real
  products: quantity-related keys returned are `inventory`, `minOrderQuantity`, `stepQuantity`.
  `maxOrderQuantity` absent.
- Custom attributes returned (so `c_*` exposure is working): `c_ap21Category`, `c_careInstructions`,
  `c_countryOfOrigin`, `c_environmentalNotes`, `c_fabricComposition`, `c_hsCode`, `c_isFinalSale`,
  `c_isNew`, `c_isSale`, `c_label`, `c_relatedMasterProductID`, `c_season`, `c_sizeFit`,
  `c_sizeGuide`, `c_styleId`, `c_styleNumber`, `c_stylingNotes`, `c_relatedSwatches`,
  `c_showEnvironmentalNote`. **None is a max-quantity attribute.**
- **Caveat:** dev sandbox only, 2 products. A custom attribute on sit/uat is not ruled out — but
  with no standard field at all, unlikely.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:123`:
  `/** Frontend-enforced limit (SFCC-196). SFCC has no platform max-order-quantity field. */`
  `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3;` — passed to `ProductView` as `maxOrderQuantity` at line 1282.
- **Conflict to record:** SFCC-268 "PDP – Maximum Purchase Quantity – **BM Config**" is
  *Ready for SIT* (Done, Sprint 3, Victor Crisostomo). Nothing reachable from the Shopper API was
  configured. 250's ACs all say "the **configured** maximum of 3".

### 2.2 The existing PDP enforcement shape (reusable)

`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`, `isMaxOrderQtyReached`:
```
if (maxOrderQuantity == null) return false;          // null = unrestricted
const inBag = basketProductItems
  .filter((item) => item.productId === productId)     // per SKU
  .reduce((sum, item) => sum + (item.quantity ?? 0), 0);  // summed ACROSS line items
return inBag >= maxOrderQuantity;                     // >=, not ==
```
Gates `handleAddToBag` (hard block) and caps `QuantityPicker`'s `max`. Tests/stories at 2, 3, null.
Note it **sums across line items** — i.e. the existing code already assumes one SKU can occupy more
than one line.

### 2.3 Basket merge: mode, default, and the same-product match rules

`mergeBasket` request parameter `productItemMergeMode`:
`"higher_quantity" | "sum_quantities" | "saved_quantity" | "separate_item"`.
SDK doc: *"By default, the higher of the two basket quantities is used for each product."*

Same-product match requires **all** of these to be equal:
> shipment · productId · option values · wishlist reference · inventory list id ·
> gift flag & message · ad-hoc price adjustments

> *"If any of the listed values don't match, then the item in the previous shopper's basket is
> copied to a **new line item** in the current shopper's basket."*

Consequence: `higher_quantity` protects only the single-line case. Two lines of the same SKU that
differ on shipment / inventory list / gift flag do **not** merge, and their quantities coexist —
so a SKU total can exceed the cap without any single line doing so. For Zimmermann the realistic
differentiators are **Collect in Boutique** (separate shipment) and **boutique vs warehouse
inventory lists** (CAI-022). At plain cart with no fulfilment choice made, both baskets sit in the
same default shipment and inventory list, so they DO match and 2 + 2 → 2 under the default.

### 2.4 Where merge is called, and with what

Four base call sites, **all passing only `createDestinationBasket: true`** (no merge mode):
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.js`
- `.../app/pages/login/index.jsx`
- `.../app/pages/social-login-redirect/index.jsx`
- `.../app/pages/checkout/partials/contact-info.jsx`

`use-auth-modal.js` carries the comment *"if you change logic here, also change it in login page"* —
Salesforce knows the invariant is duplicated.

**The invariant is login-only, deliberately not register:**
> *"we only want to merge basket when the user is logged in as a recurring user — only recurring
> users trigger the login mutation, new user triggers register mutation"*

Reason holds: a brand-new customer has no prior basket, so their guest basket simply becomes theirs.

### 2.5 No Zimmermann code merges baskets, and one route is a defect

- `grep -rn "mergeBasket" overrides/` → **empty.**
- `commerce-sdk-react` contains `mergeBasket` only as a mutation definition
  (`hooks/ShopperBaskets/mutation.js`), never in `auth/` — **the SDK does not auto-merge on login.**

`useWishlistAuthDrawer`'s three auth routes:

| Route | Merges? | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Social IDP (`AuthorizeIDP`) | Yes — redirects through base `social-login-redirect`, which merges | ✅ fine |
| Create account (`useAuthModal(REGISTER_VIEW)`) | No — base deliberately skips register | ✅ correct by design |
| **Passwordless OTP (`LoginPasswordlessUser`)** | **No** | ❌ **DEFECT** |

Passwordless OTP is a recurring-user login, which is exactly the case the invariant exists for.
Base `use-auth-modal` has its own passwordless flow **and pairs it with the merge**;
`useWishlistAuthDrawer` reimplemented passwordless login for the drawer and did not carry the merge
across. Without a merge, SLAS switches the session to the registered customer and the guest basket
is orphaned — **the shopper's items are lost, not mis-counted.**

Affects all four consumers of the hook: the cart (new), `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`,
`product-view`.

**This is code-inferred, not yet observed live. Verify before filing** — guest adds an item, opens
the cart, signs in with the email code, check whether the item survives.

### 2.6 `PendingWishlistIntent` carries no product

`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`:
`type PendingWishlistIntent = { intentId: string; timestamp: number }`, session-stored under
`zimmPendingWishlistAction`, 5-minute max age, scoped by `intentId` so only the initiating instance
replays. Fine for the three existing callers (a PDP has one product; the header's action isn't
product-specific). **The cart is the first caller with N products**, so on the social-redirect route
the resumed `onAuthSuccess` has no idea which line item the shopper clicked.

### 2.7 No cart overrides exist at all

Absent: `overrides/app/pages/cart`, `overrides/app/components/cart`,
`overrides/app/components/order-summary`, `overrides/app/components/product-item`.
`overrides/app/pages/checkout` exists but contains only `partials/payment.tsx` + its story —
`contact-info` is **not** overridden.
No `overrides/app/pages/login` — base login page still in use.

### 2.8 Order summary updates for free

Base `pages/cart/index.jsx` calls `useCurrentBasket()`, mutates via
`updateItemInBasketMutation.mutateAsync`, and passes the same basket object to `<OrderSummary>`.
So "order summary updates when quantity changes" is a consequence of basket cache invalidation, not
code any stepper story owns. Base `components/order-summary/index.jsx` exists and has no override —
so SFCC-274 is "restyle it to Figma", not "build one that doesn't exist".

### 2.9 Base `product-item` is a shared SFCC internal

Imported by `components/product-item-list`, `pages/account/wishlist`, `pages/cart`.
`protectedFiles.md` puts `overrides/app/components/product-item/` at **Tier 2, Squad B-owned
(notify Squad A)**.

### 2.10 Base wishlist handler silently no-ops for guests

`pages/cart/index.jsx`, `handleAddToWishlist`:
```
if (!customerId || !wishlist) { return }
```
A guest clicking Move to Wishlist gets **nothing**. `cart.md` §2 (CAI-008) requires the opposite:
*"an unauthenticated user selecting Move to Wishlist is prompted to log in first."*
The same handler already implements the `isItemInWishlist` branch and surfaces success via a Chakra
toast (`TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST`) with a "View Wishlist" action button.

### 2.11 ZimmButton variants and the 24px target size

Variants: `primary`, `primaryInverse`, `secondary`, `secondaryInverse`, `social`, `icon`,
`iconInverse`. Sizes: `lg`, `sm`, `social`, `icon`.
`sizes.icon` = `minW`/`minH: var(--zimm-scale-xl)`; `spacing.ts` resolves `xl` to `1.5rem` = **24px**,
chosen deliberately — the inline comment reads *"WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 — 24px minimum target size.
SFCC-55's accessibility note names this control specifically."* It also explains why it is
`minW`/`minH` and not padding: Chakra's `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0` as a style prop, so
padding declared in the recipe is silently discarded (a previous `p: 'xs'` rendered 16×16).

`actionSizes.height` = `lg: 52px`, `md: 40px` (Figma-confirmed).
**`overrideStyling.md` is stale here:** it still cites `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`
as standing provisional exceptions. Those constants no longer exist in `zimmButton.css.ts`; the only
remaining provisional is `BTN_MIN_WIDTH_LG = '80px' // audit-allow: provisional`.

### 2.12 Domestic vs international is already modelled

`overrides/app/config/countries.ts`, `CountryConfig`:
`urlSlug`, `sfccSiteId`, `locale`, `currency`, `shippingCountry`, `checkoutOwner`, `globalEPricing`,
`boutiqueRegion`. `checkoutOwner`'s own doc comment:
> *"Checkout owner for this site's domestic path. Branch checkout AND pricing logic from this field
> at PDP/cart level — not only at the checkout page."*

Read via `overrides/app/hooks/useCountryConfig.ts` (matches on `sfccSiteId` + locale to disambiguate
the en-GB collision between the UK site and EU English; falls back to AU on an unrecognised site).

### 2.13 Base Checkout CTA has no region branch

`pages/cart/partials/cart-cta.jsx` → `<Button as={Link} to="/checkout">` unconditionally.
So international shoppers already land on SFCC checkout today; leaving that path alone is the
current behaviour, not a regression. The same file also uses `useExpressCheckoutEnabled()`, which
already gates express buttons on the cart — worth checking before writing new show/hide logic.

### 2.14 Empty-state precedent

`overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` (on `origin/feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed-einstein`,
PR #116 — **not merged to develop**). Pattern, per its own JSDoc: structure ported from base
`EmptyCart` (`pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`) as `Box > Center > Stack`; `isRegistered`-branched
body copy; `Button as={Link}` using the **base SFCC `Link`** (not raw react-router) so the CTA href
gets multi-site prefixing via `use-multi-site`'s `buildUrl`; `useIntl` called directly in the leaf
under the Context-backed exception in `components.md`; private single-parent sub-component so no
story/test of its own; decision log at the bottom of the file.

That file made **autonomous styling judgement calls** because it had no design at all. The cart
does have one (SFCC-315 carries an Empty Cart screenshot), so take **structure** from the precedent
and **visuals from Figma** — do not repeat the token-invention.

### 2.15 House pattern for a design-vs-standard deviation

From `zimmButton.css.ts`: cite the specific criterion, name where the requirement came from, explain
any mechanical gotcha, and name what is deferred and who owns it. Examples in that file: the 2.5.8
note above, and the focus-ring block — *"Replaces the previous outline:none + bg-swap, which gave the
primary variant an invisible focus state (#191919 default vs #000000 focus) — a WCAG 2.4.7 failure...
Dark-surface / inverse ring (grey-white) is the separate deferred inverse-focus item, owned with the
UI designer."*

**Annotate inline, log with the designer, ship. Do not escalate or block.**

---

## 3. A reading correction worth keeping

I over-read cross-references three times in this session. A `see SFCC-NNN` / "Relates to" in an AC
usually points at **where the design or detail lives**, not at a gate. Treat it as a dependency only
when the card says so outright — as SFCC-272's description does (*"This story is dependent on other
components being developed, including..."*) and SFCC-250's does (*"The following components must be
developed before this story can be implemented end to end"*).

Wrongly called blocked and later corrected: SFCC-271 (on 274), SFCC-275 (on 816), and AC2 of
SFCC-272 (on 277).

---

## 4. Per-card decisions

### SFCC-315 — Drawer (Cart Variation) · 9 ACs · all buildable

ACs: header `"BAG • [count]"` with right-aligned X / `"YOUR BAG IS EMPTY"` when empty; count updates
dynamically without reload; slides in from the right, right portion on desktop+tablet with a
non-interactive overlaid background, **full screen on mobile**; closes via X, outside click, and
Escape with **focus returned to the trigger**; no loss of page state or scroll position on close;
responsive per Figma.

- Build as a **new organism wrapping `ZimmDrawer`**, not as a modification to the atom and not as an
  override of base `pages/cart`.
- Reuse: `ZimmDrawer` already has `finalFocusRef` (AC7), the overlay, right placement, size variants,
  mobile full-height, and concurrent-instance scroll-lock coordination — all from SFCC-831/926.
- AC3's dynamic count comes free from basket cache invalidation.
- AC8: verify the scroll-lock **restores** position on close rather than merely unlocking.
- **315 owns the empty-state *header text* only.** The empty *body* is SFCC-277's. Clean split.
- 315 is a dependency for SFCC-270, 274, 316, 318, 404 — and **SFCC-316 (Zimmermann Benefits –
  Contentful) is Sprint 5, Ready for Development, assigned to Jhoan Rose Dela Cruz.** Someone else's
  active-sprint card is waiting on this. **Ship 315 first and standalone.**

### SFCC-270 — Cart Item UI Part 1 · 9 ACs · all buildable

ACs: per line item — image; name to the right of the image; price; selected colour; selected size;
quantity with `+`/`–` either side; multiple items each individually identifiable; Remove and Wishlist
as **underlined text links below the stepper**; on mobile nothing truncated or hidden.

**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): override base `product-item`.** Cart keeps using it. Separately,
upcoming wishlist work moves the account wishlist page onto `ZimmProductCard` (which already has a
`variation: 'wishlist'` with `showRemove`), so it stops consuming `product-item` at that point.

Accurate consumer map — **two chains only**:
```
pages/cart  ->  components/product-item-list  ->  components/product-item
pages/account/wishlist  ->  components/product-item          (direct)
```
Checkout does **not** use it. The base has two separate line-item systems: `product-item` (the full
interactive row) and `item-variant/*` (a read-only composition used by `order-summary`, i.e. the
checkout summaries).

**Copy-first scope — 3 files** from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/`:
`index.jsx` (7.4 KB), `bonus-product-quantity.jsx` (1.5 KB), `product-quantity-picker.jsx` (3.4 KB),
each to `.tsx`. Base's own `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` are not copied — write our own.

**The finding that changes the size of the job:** `product-item/index.jsx` renders its visible content
through **five more base components** — `components/item-variant` plus `item-variant/item-image`,
`item-name`, `item-attributes`, `item-price`. So overriding `product-item` gives you the row's
*structure and controls*; the *content pieces* still come from `item-variant/*`. Styling those to
Figma means either overriding `item-variant/*` too — which also changes `order-summary`, and
therefore the checkout summaries — or not using them inside our override and composing the content
ourselves. **Decide this before starting: it is the difference between a 3-file override and an
8-file one with checkout blast radius.**

**`shared/ui` barrel trap applies.** `product-item/index.jsx` imports from `components/shared/ui`.
Per the known trap, overriding an individual `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing — 208 base files
import the barrel, so only overriding the barrel itself has any effect.

**Bridge-pattern requirement:** because `product-item` is used internally by base components, the
override's **default export must stay API-compatible** (full original prop surface) so
`product-item-list` and the wishlist page keep working. Per `overrideStyling.md`, put brand styling
in a **theme recipe**, not a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't need the second
export that `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.

**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): Option B — override `item-variant/*` as well. 8 files.**
`product-item/{index,bonus-product-quantity,product-quantity-picker}` +
`item-variant/{index,item-image,item-name,item-attributes,item-price}`, all to `.tsx`.

Verified before deciding: **every consumer of `item-variant/*` is base/OOTB with no Zimmermann
design or development**, so brand styling landing on them is an upgrade toward Zimmermann, not a
regression from it. Full consumer list — `components/order-summary` (no override),
`components/multiship/multiship-order-summary`, `pages/account/order-detail` (account has zero
overrides), `pages/account/wishlist/partials/wishlist-primary-action` +
`wishlist-secondary-button-group` (and wishlist is migrating to `ZimmProductCard` anyway),
`pages/cart/partials/cart-secondary-button-group` (base cart page, replaced by the drawer),
`pages/checkout/partials/{pickup-address,product-shipping-address-card,shipping-product-cards}`
(checkout override is only `payment.tsx`), `pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-product-shipping-address-card`.

**`pages/confirmation` is NOT in the blast radius** — `overrides/app/pages/confirmation/index.tsx`
already exists and does not use `item-variant`, so the base confirmation page is shadowed and never
renders. That was the one surface worth worrying about (a shopper sees it after paying).

**Two requirements for the override, both load-bearing:**
1. **Keep the defaults-then-spread order.** Callers set their own geometry —
   `order-summary` does `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` — and must keep winning.
   Write `<Box width={zimmDefault} {...props}>`, never the reverse, or you break layouts that work
   today. `item-image`, `item-attributes` and `item-price` already have it right.
2. **Fix `item-name` while in there.** Base is `<Link {...props} color="black.600">` — spread
   *before* the colour, so no caller can ever override it. Move the spread after; no base caller
   passes `color`, so nothing changes for them.

**Deferred consequence, accepted:** when checkout is designed it will inherit cart-derived
line-item styling it never specified. Whoever picks up checkout should know why it already looks
part-branded.

**Governance:** `overrides/app/components/product-item/` is **Tier 2, Squad B-owned (notify Squad A)**
per `protectedFiles.md`. CODEOWNERS will request Squad B's review on a Squad A ticket.

**Interim consequence, low risk:** while the account wishlist page still consumes `product-item`, our
override's styling reaches it too. `overrides/app/pages/` contains no account pages at all — account
is entirely base and unstyled today — so the exposure is minimal until the wishlist migration lands.

### SFCC-271 — Quantity Stepper · 4 ACs · all buildable

ACs: `+` increments by 1 with item total and order summary updating; `–` decrements when quantity > 1;
at quantity 1 the `–` is disabled and quantity stays 1; drawer count (`Bag 3`) and order summary both
update without a full page load.

- **No SFCC-274 dependency** — see §2.8. Deliverable is the mutation call, the debounce, the
  optimistic local quantity, and the error rollback. The summary updating falls out of invalidation.

### SFCC-250 — Maximum Purchase Quantity · 9 ACs · 9 of 9 addressed

The rule: **max 3 units per SKU (same size + colour) per order** — CAI-017, `cart.md` §2.
The card states outright it is *not* a component build story: the stepper is 271's, the inline
warning is 795's, the page-level banner is 404's.

| Decision | Value |
|---|---|
| Max value | No BM setting exists (§2.1). Promote `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` out of `product-detail/index.tsx:123` into a shared constant; cart reads the same one. Re-typing `3` would breach `conventions.md`'s no-magic-numbers rule. |
| Threshold | **`>=`**, not the AC's literal "equals" — otherwise a line already holding 4 fails the check and the `+` stays live exactly when it matters. Matches the PDP. |
| Scope of the limit | **Per line item.** Rationale: the SKU is already size *and* colour, so in normal shopping one line **is** one SKU. |
| Merge mode | **`sum_quantities`.** AC5's "combined quantity ... exceeds the maximum" only works if quantities add. |
| Cap shape | **Consolidate to one line at 3.** Free — `sum_quantities` already produces a single *"merged line item"* for matching products. |
| Merge call | **Zimmermann-owned**, placed where `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync` succeeds in `useWishlistAuthDrawer` — completing the half-implemented pairing in §2.5, and covering all four consumers at once. |
| Callback order | **merge → cap → 272's pending wishlist resume.** The wishlist move acts on a line the merge may have just consolidated and the cap just reduced; reversing the order moves a quantity the shopper never saw. |
| Render guard | Secondary backstop for baskets that went over some other way (stale session, order-on-behalf). **No-ops while any basket mutation is in flight** via React Query's `useIsMutating()`, so it cannot race the callback. |
| Shared logic | Merge-and-cap lives in **its own small function**, called by both the callback and the render guard — one implementation, not two copies. |
| Flash (briefly showing 4) | **No action.** Observe the real behaviour first. |
| Loop guard | **Keep it** — distinct from the flash. Without it, a write-on-render can fire repeatedly (concurrent writes racing on one line item; or endless retries if the server refuses), which can rate-limit a shopper out of their own basket. One correction in flight, one attempt per basket version, then stop and surface an error. |

AC disposition: **1, 2** build (needs 271, 795) · **3, 8** → SFCC-404 · **4, 9** nothing to build
(negative assertions; Apple/Google Pay buttons don't exist yet anyway) · **5** build ·
**6, 7** free — they are AC1 and AC2's rules applied to a post-merge state, and a consolidated line
at 3 satisfies per-line `>=`.

**Accepted consequence of `sum_quantities`, recorded deliberately:** it changes **every** merge, not
just over-max ones. A guest adds one dress, signs in a week later, the account already had it —
today they get one, with summing they get two. Marcel accepted this explicitly. **It must go in a
comment on the card**, because no AC describes it and a tester finding it otherwise has no way to
know two items is intended rather than a bug.

**Deliberate boundary, recorded so it isn't mistaken for an oversight:** per-line enforcement means
a SKU split across two lines can total more than 3 without either line hitting max. That case only
arises from the merge splitting a line, which is what AC5 exists to catch. In that same edge case the
PDP (which sums per SKU) and the cart (per line) apply different rules.

`Recommended-for-you` swaps its heading to **"SHOP THE LOOK"** for signed-out shoppers — so a
**non-personalised fallback exists that does not need Einstein** (relevant: Einstein is Not
Deployed on all 8 sites).

## 11.7 Empty bag (SFCC-315 AC2 / SFCC-277)

Layout **changes**, not just copy: Cart-item-group -> 360x157; **Totals summary moves x=500 -> x=0**
and shrinks 430x857 -> **430x263** at y=297. Two columns collapse to one.
- "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY" is in the **header**, not the body
- the body is **Client Services contact copy**: "If you'd like some help, speak to one of our Client
  Services Advisors at: / +61 1800 738 895 / Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM / or
  clientservices@zimmermann.com" (email underlined)
- `Default/Body 1` Futura Round Regular 16px / lh 24 / ls **-0.16px**; paragraph spacing
  `mb-[25px]` (RAW)
- **AU phone number and AU opening hours are hardcoded in the design** — must vary per storefront
  across 8 sites. No AC covers this.

## 11.8 Touch targets — Figma is internally inconsistent

| Element | Wrapper | Icon |
|---|---|---|
| Cart-level-message | named `touchTarget` **24x24** | 20 |
| Recommended-for-you chevrons | **24x24** | 16 |
| drawer/header close | **44h x 24w** | 16 |
| **Cart item stepper +/-** | **none** | **12** |

"44" has provenance (close-button height) but **nothing in the design is 44x44**, which is what
SFCC-795's AC asks for. And the stepper has no touch target at all — 12px, half the 24px the rest
of the system uses. Per the house pattern (`zimmButton.css.ts`): annotate inline citing the
criterion and the source, add to the UI designer's open list, ship. Also **ask the designer whether
the stepper icons should get the same 24px touchTarget** — it reads as an oversight, not intent.

## 11.9 Design-side issues to raise

- stepper icons 12px with no touch target, against a 24px system convention
- `25px` used twice as an untokenised raw value (Item Actions gap; empty-bag paragraph spacing)
- two token namespaces coexist: `brand/font/*` + `alias/*` vs `default/*` + `line-height/*`
- two tokens resolve to the same #969696 (`text/subtlest` vs `text/muted`)
- stacked success drops the product name; single success keeps it
- SFCC-272 copy conflicts: design "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist" vs AC "[Product Name]
  has been moved to your wishlist"; design already-in-wishlist is a **warning** ("An item in your
  bag already exists in Wishlist") vs AC's **error** banner with different wording.
  Cards say "figma leading" => design wins, but record the divergence on 272.
- ~~empty-bag Client Services details are hardcoded AU~~ — **NOT an issue for this build**
  (Marcel, 2026-09-16): we ship a placeholder empty state only; the real one is SFCC-277's.
  **But the question carries to SFCC-277** — the design hardcodes `+61 1800 738 895`,
  "Monday – Saturday: 9:00AM – 5:30PM" and `clientservices@zimmermann.com` across 8 storefronts /
  6 regions. Which of those vary per region, and are hours shown in local or AU time?
  Flag on 277 at grooming so it isn't rediscovered mid-build.

## 11.10 Design open items — RESOLVED (2026-09-16)

**(4) `25px` raw value — DECIDED (Marcel): implement 24px** (`--zimm-scale-xl`… actually
`space/600`), with a short comment noting the design specified 25 and it was snapped to the nearest
tokenised value. Applies to the Item Actions gap and the empty-bag paragraph spacing.

**(5) Two token namespaces — RESOLVED from the codebase.** Our `--zimm-font-*` vars mirror
`brand/font/*`'s shape (family / size / lineheight / letterspacing), not `default/*` +
`line-height/*`. So `brand/font/*` is the current generation; the `default/*` usages (empty-bag
body, promo accordion) are the older one.
**More useful: our 22 registered textStyles map near 1:1 to the Figma named styles** — map style→
textStyle, not var-by-var:
`Default/body2`→`body2` · `body2-strong`→`body2Strong` · `Caption`→`caption` ·
`Link-sm`→`linkSm` · `Product-name`/`Product Names`→`productNames` · `Price`→`price` ·
`Button-lg`→`button` · `Body 1`→`body1` · `Body 2 Medium`→`body2Strong`
**Two gaps:** no `captionStrong` for Figma's `Default/Caption-strong` (the cart item's colour+size
line, medium/500) — we only have `caption`. And `mobileBody1`/`mobileBody2`/`mobileBody1Strong`
exist, so there are mobile-specific styles to consider for the reflow.

**(6) Two tokens for #969696 — RESOLVED from the codebase.** We have
`text.muted = grey[300] = #969696` and **no `subtlest`**. Both Figma names collapse onto
**`--zimm-color-text-muted`**. No ambiguity in our system.
**Bonus — every colour in the cart design already exists in our foundation. No new tokens needed:**
| Figma | Ours |
|---|---|
| `text/default` #191919 | `grey[900]` → `--zimm-color-text-default` |
| `text/subtle` #666 | `grey[600]` → `text.secondary` |
| `text/subtlest` + `text/muted` #969696 | `grey[300]` → `text.muted` |
| `text/error` #9c0000 | `red[500]` → **`status.error`** |
| `text/success` #2d5a3d | `green[500]` → **`status.success`** |
| `bg/surface/default` #f6f4f1 | `ivory[200]` |
| `border/default` #e6e6e6 | `grey[100]` → `border.default` |

**(7) Warning typography — DRIFT, conclusively.** Checked desktop + mobile. The WARNINGS SHOWN
state is off-pattern in **four** ways at both breakpoints:
- `Default/Body 2 Medium` (Medium/500, ls −0.14px) vs every other message's `Default/body2`
  (regular/400, ls 0)
- **`px-[128px]` hardcoded** instead of `var(--alias/space/3200)` — and it is on a **mobile** frame
  where the gutter should be 32px
- **`text-[#969696]` hardcoded hex** instead of the token var
- `Page-level-message` `w-full` instead of the established `w-[476px]`
Its mobile header is also 68px where the default mobile frame's is 108px.
=> built separately, off-pattern. **Implement WARNINGS SHOWN using the established message pattern**
   (body2, `--zimm-color-text-muted`, tokenised gutter), not its own styling.

**(8) Stacked success drops the product name — INTENTIONAL by prevalence.** Generic
("Item added to Wishlist") at **both** desktop and mobile in the stacked state; product-named
("Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist") in the single state. Consistent in both states, so per
the one-off-vs-prevalent test it is deliberate compaction.
**But worth confirming rather than silently following:** it drops the single most useful piece of
information exactly when there is more on screen, and it conflicts with SFCC-272's AC, which
specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases.

**(9) Odd computed numbers — ROOT FOUND. Two separate causes.**
- **The decimal paddings are post-scale rendered values of real tokens.** Proof: `alias/space/1200`
  reports fallback **48px** on the empty-bag cart-item-group gap and **12.655px** on the cart item
  image; `alias/space/1000` reports **40px** on the header/recommendations and **8.944px** on the
  mobile cart item image. Same token, different fallback => the decimal is what Figma rendered after
  scaling, not the token value. **Use the token (48 / 40), never the decimal.**
- **Tablet 659.2 is a computed fill width, not a spec.** `659.2 = 595.2 content + 2 × 32 gutter`;
  the gutter is a real token (32px). Confirmed NOT a uniformly scaled instance — the tablet header
  is its own 92px and the message band is exactly 52 (unscaled).
  **Implement tablet as a fluid width with a 32px gutter, never a hardcoded 659.2.**

### Responsive rule (derived)
| | Panel | Layout | Gutter | Header |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Desktop 1440+ | **fixed 1186px** | two-column (items 360 / totals 430, 140 gutter) | 128 | 84 |
| Tablet 834 | fluid (~79%) | **single column** | **32** | 92 |
| Mobile 402 | full-width | single column | 32 | 108 (68 in some states — drift) |

### Additional drift found while resolving these
- **The mobile message band hardcodes `px-[128px]` across multiple states** — should be 32px.
  Systematic, not a one-off.
- **Mobile header height varies by state**: 108 (default) vs 68 (error states).
- **Within a single node, one message is `w-full` and the next is `w-[476px]`** (mobile
  warnings-hidden). Clear drift.

## 11.11 Final three design items — SETTLED (Marcel, 2026-09-16). None go to the designer as questions.

**(1) Stepper touch target — BUILD 24px.** Wrap each 12x12 glyph in an invisible 24x24 centred box.
Justified three ways independently: our own atoms already use 24 (`zimmButton`, `zimmTextInput`,
`zimmNavItem`, `footerNavColumn` — all `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`), the design's own node is literally
named `touchTarget` at 24, and WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8 sets 24 as the minimum (AGENTS.md targets 2.2 AA).
Use `ZimmButton`'s `icon` size — it is already `minW`/`minH: var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, and its comment
explains why it must be minW/minH rather than padding (Chakra `IconButton` hard-sets `padding: 0`
as a style prop that merges after `__css`, so recipe padding is silently dropped).
**Gap: use 8px (`xs`)** -> 14px apparent, since a 24 box adds 6px invisible padding each side and
there is no 6px token (scale jumps 4 -> 8 -> 12). 4 and 8 are equidistant from the design's 12;
8 is chosen because erring toward more space is correct for a touch control.
Annotate: design showed a 12px glyph with no touch target and a 12px gap; we applied the system's 24.

**(2) Stacked success message — FOLLOW THE DESIGN: drop the product name when other messages are
present.** Single message -> "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist". Stacked -> "Item added to
Wishlist". (Marcel overrode the recommendation to keep the name in both cases.)
**Two consequences to build for:**
- The copy is **two strings selected by stack state**, not one string with a placeholder. The
  message emitter must know whether other messages are present to choose. That couples copy
  selection to the aggregator's state — a real requirement for SFCC-404.
- **The interim Chakra toast uses the product-named copy.** A toast has no aggregation concept and
  is always "on its own" from the shopper's point of view; the generic variant only becomes
  reachable once 404 lands with real stacking.
- Diverges from SFCC-272's AC, which specifies `[Product Name]` in all cases. Cards are "figma
  leading" and are not edited -> record on the 272 comment.

**(3) Mobile drift — use our own values, not the drifted nodes.**
- gutter on mobile -> **32px** (the 128px in those nodes is the desktop value left on a mobile frame)
- message width on mobile -> **full width** (476px is the desktop value; it is wider than the 402
  viewport)
- header height -> **whatever `ZimmDrawer` already implements**. Its header sizing was reconciled
  against Figma during SFCC-831/926, so it has already been through the designer. Do NOT re-derive
  from these nodes, which disagree with each other (108 vs 68).

**Nothing in §11.9–11.11 blocks the build, and NO message goes to the UI designer** — Marcel,
2026-09-16: these sit within the developer's own decisions. The divergences are handled by
annotating inline at the point of use, per the house pattern in `zimmButton.css.ts` (cite the
criterion, name the source, say what was applied and why). §11.9's list stays as a record of what
was found, not as an open action on anyone.

### B1 — SFCC-315, cart drawer organism

#### Step 1.1 — Fix `ZimmDrawer`'s `xLarge` width (this is a real bug, not a tidy-up)

**Consequence first.** `zimmDrawer.css.ts` already ships an `xLarge` size whose own comment says it is for Cart. Its value is `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'`. Figma's cart panel is a **fixed 1186px** at both 1440 and 1920 (§11.1; panel `x=256` on the 1440 frame and `x=736` on the 1920 frame — 1184 both times, so the *gap* grows and the panel does not). 82% of 1920 is **1574px** — 388px wider than designed. The inner composition is itself fixed (128 + 360 + 140 + 430 + 128 = 1186), so on a 1920 screen the shopper gets 388px of dead white space inside the panel, and the two-column layout sits off-centre. Build SFCC-315 on the existing variant unchanged and it is wrong on every large monitor.

**Mechanism.** The 82% came from a Figma frame annotation, and `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s own comment records that the *previous* reading of that same annotation was already wrong once ("that frame's annotation was wrong (or superseded)"). The annotation is a percentage; the frames are a fixed width.

**Changes.** Replace `WIDTH_XLARGE = '82%'` with a rem constant equal to 1186px (`74.125rem`), applied as `width`/`maxWidth` with `maxWidth: '100%'` so it cannot exceed a narrow viewport. Keep the comment convention: cite the Figma frames, state that 82% was the annotation and 1186 is the measurement, per the `zimmButton.css.ts` house pattern.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `zimmDrawer.css.test.ts` gains an assertion that `xLarge.content` resolves to the 1186px rem value above `md`, and that `maxWidth` is `100%`.
2. No other size variant's resolved output changes — assert `large`, `tablet`, `small`, `prompt`, `mobile` snapshots are byte-identical to before.
3. `grep -rn "xLarge" overrides/app --include="*.tsx"` returns only `index.tsx`'s type union and `index.stories.tsx` — **confirmed zero production consumers today**, so blast radius is nil. Re-run this before committing; if a consumer has appeared, stop.
4. `npm run audit:tokens` does not flag the new rem constant (it carries a `// audit-allow:` or `provisional` comment naming the Figma frame, matching `PANEL_MIN_NARROW`'s existing treatment in the same file).

**Changes.** New organism at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/`, wrapping `ZimmDrawer` with `size="xLarge"`. Props only — `isOpen`, `onClose`, `itemCount`, `finalFocusRef`, `children`, plus a `messages` slot and a `footer` slot (the footer slot is what hosts SFCC-275's button group until SFCC-816 lands). Recipe `ZimmCartDrawer` with parts for the messages band, the content container, and the two-column/one-column grid.

Header title: `"BAG • {count}"` via `ZimmDrawer`'s existing `title` prop (AC1). Empty: `"YOUR BAG IS EMPTY"` — **header text only**; the empty *body* is SFCC-277's and arrives in B4 as a slotted component.

**Changes.** New atom, variant-driven: `error` (`status.error`) / `warning` (`text.muted`). It sits **between the stepper and the actions row**, full width, `textStyle="caption"` with weight overridden to regular per gate #13. In error states the Item Details gap widens 12 → 16px — that is a recipe state on `ZimmCartItem`, not a prop on the message.

**Presentation only.** OOS / partial OOS triggering is SFCC-282 and Unavailable is SFCC-796 — both Sprint 6, Hazel's. Build prop-driven with stories; do not wire detection logic.

Copy, verbatim from Figma: fully OOS **"This item is unavailable"**; partial OOS **"Quantity unavailable in this size"**; max quantity **"Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size"**.

Per gate #4, max-quantity renders as the **warning** variant (grey, `text.muted`), not error — the design and SFCC-250 AC4 agree; CAI-017's word "error" means user-facing feedback, not the severity tier. Annotate that reconciliation inline.

Per gate #9, **there is no low-stock variant** — CAI-030 forbids low-stock messaging at cart level. Do not add one.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Stories: `Error`, `Warning`, plus one per copy string above. Each renders the exact copy.
2. `error` resolves to `var(--zimm-color-status-error)`; `warning` to `var(--zimm-color-text-muted)`. Both asserted in the recipe test against the token var, not a hex.
3. The organism recipe test asserts Item Details gap is the 12px token by default and the 16px token in the error state.
4. Message renders in DOM order **between** stepper and actions.
5. No `#9c0000`, `#969696` or any hex literal in either file — `npm run audit:tokens` clean.
6. No low-stock variant exists in the component's variant union.

#### Step 3.3 — Promotional price + discount label

**Changes.** The was/now mechanism **already exists** in base `display-price` (`priceData` with `listPrice`/`currentPrice`/`isOnSale`, renders `ListPrice` struck, already multiplies by quantity so it is line-item aware). Only the **discount label** ("20% off applied") is new, and it is purely presentational — prop-driven, storied, wired when the promotions engine lands. It renders beneath the stepper.

`display-price` has **no override** and is a shared SFCC internal. Do not override it in this step; if Zimmermann styling is needed later it goes through the bridge pattern (faithful default export, styling in a recipe).

**Pass criteria.**
1. With `isOnSale` and a `listPrice`, the struck "Was" and the "Now" both render, and both scale with quantity.
2. With a `discountLabel` prop, the label renders beneath the stepper; without it, no empty node is emitted.
3. `git status` shows no new file under `overrides/app/components/display-price/`.

#### Step 3.4 — `cartItemMapper` + `maxOrderQuantity` util

**Changes.** `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartItemMapper.ts` converts an SDK basket `productItem` to the override's props — the `productListCardMapper.ts` precedent from PR #85. This is what keeps every component in B3 prop-driven with no data-fetching hook in a leaf. `useIntl` is permitted in leaves (Context-backed exception); nothing else is.

`overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts` reads **`c_maxOrderQuantity` off the SCAPI product response with a fallback of 3** — gate finding #1. Do **not** promote `MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY` out of `product-detail/index.tsx:123` into a shared constant: the TSD for SFCC-268 shows a real BM site preference surfaced as `c_maxOrderQuantity` via an `afterGET` hook, with resolution order product override (SFCC-703) → site preference → hardcoded 3. Reading the field with a fallback degrades to today's behaviour when absent and picks up the real value the day the hook ships. A shared constant would need reworking then.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `maxOrderQuantity.test.ts` covers: `c_maxOrderQuantity` present → returns it; absent → returns 3; present but `0`, negative, or non-numeric → returns 3 (fallback, not a broken cap).
2. `cartItemMapper.test.ts` covers: full line item → all props; missing image → no crash and an `alt` still present; colour and size → **one** combined string in the documented order; quantity and `stepQuantity` passed through.
3. `grep -rn "useCurrentBasket\|useProduct\|commerce-sdk-react" overrides/app/components/ui-kits/**/zimmCart* overrides/app/components/product-item overrides/app/components/item-variant` returns **nothing**.
4. No `const MAX_PURCHASE_QUANTITY = 3` typed anywhere new (no-magic-numbers), and `product-detail/index.tsx` is **not** modified — that is Squad B's file and refactoring upward is Hard Rule #5.

#### Step 3.5 — Wire `ZimmQuantityStepper` + `maxOrderQuantity` into `product-item` (inserted 2026-09-18)

**Why this step exists.** Not in the original plan. Found during the SFCC-795 accessibility sweep (originally step 3.5, now 3.6): `product-item/index.tsx` still renders base `ProductQuantityPicker` (unstyled base `QuantityPicker`) — `ZimmQuantityStepper` (step 3.1, commit `286deb09`) has zero production usage anywhere, and no later step in this plan ever wires it in. Confirmed by grepping the entire plan text before adding this step. Same root cause, same discovery: `maxOrderQuantity.ts` (step 3.4, commit `f2612b92`) is not plumbed into the real stepper either — no `max` is ever passed to the real, currently-rendered component, so there is no live cap enforcement anywhere today. Marcel's call (2026-09-18): plan both wirings in now rather than leave them standalone indefinitely.

**Changes.** In `product-item/index.tsx`, replace the `ProductQuantityPicker` branch (the `!product.bonusProductLineItem` case only — `BonusProductQuantity` is a separate, static display for free/bonus items and is out of this step's scope) with `ZimmQuantityStepper`. `ZimmQuantityStepper` is a controlled component (`quantity`/`min`/`max`/`isUnavailable`/`onDecrement(nextQuantity)`/`onIncrement(nextQuantity)`) — a different contract than `ProductQuantityPicker`'s `onItemQuantityChange`+`setQuantity` split, so this is real integration, not a prop rename. Keep `product-item`'s own existing `quantity`/`setQuantity` local state; wire `onDecrement`/`onIncrement` to call the same `onItemQuantityChange`-then-conditionally-`setQuantity` flow the old `handleQuantityChange` used, adapted to the new callback shape (each receives the already-computed next value directly, unlike the old picker's raw string/number input-change event).

`min={1}` — resolves the audit's own found discrepancy directly in the new stepper's favour: the old, real component floored at 0 (never actually speced or tested against ACs); `ZimmQuantityStepper` was built and tested against a floor of 1 since step 3.1 (AC3, "quantity 1: `−` is disabled"). `max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}` — the first real caller of the step 3.4 util, `product` here being the same raw object `product-item` already receives (the util's own input type accepts a product-shaped object with an optional `c_maxOrderQuantity`, satisfied structurally).

`isUnavailable` — no real OOS-detection signal exists yet (SFCC-282/796, later sprint, already established as out of this whole epic's scope). Leave unset/`false` for this step, same "presentation only, no detection logic" principle step 3.2 already established for `message`. Do not invent a detection heuristic.

**Pass criteria.**
1. `product-item/index.test.tsx`: with `product.c_maxOrderQuantity` absent, the rendered stepper's effective max resolves to 3 (the util's own fallback) — assert via the real DOM (e.g. clicking `+` from quantity 3 does nothing further, or the increment control's `aria-disabled` state at that boundary), not by asserting the util was called with the right arguments alone.
2. With `c_maxOrderQuantity: 5` on the product, the stepper allows incrementing up to 5 and no further.
3. At quantity 1, decrement is disabled (matches `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own step-3.1 tested contract, resolves the audit's floor-of-0-vs-1 finding).
4. `BonusProductQuantity`'s own render branch and props are unchanged — diff `product-item/index.tsx` and confirm nothing in that branch moved.
5. `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own existing test suite (step 3.1) still passes unmodified — this step wires an existing, already-tested component, it does not change its own contract.
6. Storybook: `product-item/index.stories.tsx`'s existing stories all still render without throwing (the swapped-in stepper needs `min`/`max`/`onDecrement`/`onIncrement`, confirm every existing story still supplies enough for it to render, adding args where a story genuinely needs them).

#### Step 3.6 — Accessibility sweep against 795's 11 a11y ACs (renumbered from 3.5, 2026-09-18 — step 3.5 above now owns the stepper-wiring gap this sweep originally found)

**Changes.** Mostly verification — the 11 accessibility ACs are each checked off explicitly, now against the *real*, newly-wired stepper from step 3.5, not the orphaned `ZimmQuantityStepper` story in isolation. One real fix included: `ZimmInlineMessage` is not programmatically associated with its line item today (DOM adjacency only, no explicit ARIA link) — Marcel's call (2026-09-18): cheap, fix it now as part of going through this checklist. Give the rendered message element a real `id` and reference it via `aria-describedby` on the quantity control it's describing (the message is about the item's quantity/availability state, which is what the stepper controls) — exact mechanism left to the implementer, following whatever pattern other associated-error-text components in this codebase (form field + validation message, if any exist) already use, or a straightforward `aria-describedby` pairing if none do.

**Pass criteria.** One checkable line per AC, enumerated in the PR body, each naming the file and the assertion that proves it. At minimum: every `IconButton` has `aria-label`; every `<img>` has `alt`; quantity changes announce via a live region — **corrected 2026-09-19, found by this step's own Scorer**: proven via `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own `<chakra.span aria-live="polite">` around the live quantity value (`zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx`), not base `product-quantity-picker.tsx`'s `VisuallyHidden role="status"` as this line originally said — see the new paragraph below on why that component is no longer part of this path at all; stepper controls reachable and operable by keyboard alone (now against the real `ZimmQuantityStepper`); focus-visible ring present and distinguishable on stepper, both action links (**`ZimmCartItemActions`/step 4.4 doesn't exist yet — unverifiable until then, not a failure of this step**), and the drawer close; the inline message is programmatically associated with its line item (**the one real fix this step makes — was a genuine gap, not just an audit false-negative**); target sizes ≥24px; no colour-only state conveyance. Storybook a11y check green on every story in B3.

**Known, disclosed, NOT fixed in this step (Tier 1 / cross-cutting, needs UI-designer sign-off, not this build's authority to resolve):** `text.muted` (`grey[300]`, `#969696`) fails WCAG AA contrast against white at the sizes this build renders it (measured 2.95:1, needs 4.5:1) — confirmed via the real Storybook a11y test-runner, not assumed. This is not new to this step or this epic: `colour.ts`'s own existing comment already flags `grey[300]` as an unresolved Handover self-contradiction (`#969696` vs `#939393` — checked: the alternate value doesn't fix the contrast problem either, both are too light). The same token is already shipped in 10+ other components across the storefront (footer, product card, product price, size chip, button, subscribe modal, icons) — this may already be a live accessibility issue outside this epic entirely, not something this step introduced. Ship to the current spec value per this repo's own established precedent for exactly this situation (`colour.ts`'s own "shipping the current value, confirm with the UI designer" comment) — raise with the UI designer post-build, do not silently drop it and do not invent a replacement value unilaterally.

**Also found by this step's own Scorer (2026-09-19), not this step's to fix:** `product-quantity-picker.tsx` (Tier 2, in B3's manifest) now has zero real callers anywhere in the app. `product-item/index.tsx` dropped its import in step 3.5/commit `c426c4ef` when `ZimmQuantityStepper` was wired in to replace it as the real interactive control, and nothing else under `overrides/` ever imported it — confirmed via `grep -rn "from '\./product-quantity-picker'" overrides/`, which returns exactly one hit, the component's own `product-quantity-picker.test.tsx`. This makes the file's previously-cited live-region defect (reads the static `product.quantity` prop, never the live value) moot for the shopper-facing UI rather than fixed — nobody sees it fire at all anymore, correct or not, since nothing renders the component. Per Hard Rule #9 (never delete a file without being explicitly asked), this build leaves it mounted-but-uncalled rather than deleting it — same shape as the base `AddToCartModal`/`/cart` page pattern this epic already carries elsewhere (see HANDOFF.md's "Settled — do not reopen"). Flagged for Marcel to decide: delete outright (Tier 2, needs the same owner sign-off as any other Tier 2 change) or leave as-is.

## Could not verify / carried forward as Outstanding

- **Resolved, not still open (commit 11's own Tester flagged this, then Marcel correctly resolved
  it against the actual AC decomposition, not the PRD's compressed summary):** the Tester found
  that hitting the new quantity cap via the stepper shows no message — just a disabled `+` button —
  and read `.docs/prd/cart.md:28`'s one-line "error displayed if exceeded" (CAI-017) as requiring
  one there too. It doesn't. `session-notes.md`'s own SFCC-250 AC disposition splits this cleanly:
  ACs 1/2 (stepper interaction, needs 271/795) are about the button's disabled state only; AC5 —
  the one whose own text is "**combined quantity** exceeds the maximum" (cited verbatim twice in
  the plan) — is the merge-correction scenario, the only case where a message is actually needed,
  because that's the only case where the shopper's cart changes without them clicking anything. The
  message is correctly scoped to step 4.2 (`useCartMergeAndCap`, not yet built), not this step. No
  new step needed; nothing was actually missing.
- FocusLock/`handleCloseComplete` race in `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` (commit 6 finding) — affects every
  `ZimmDrawer` consumer using `finalFocusRef`. Flagged, not fixed — out of this build's own scope.
- `showInventoryMessage`/`inventoryMessage` duplication risk in `product-item/index.tsx` (commit 8
  finding) — real and already live via the base hook today, but currently inert since `ProductItem`
  has no production caller yet. Needs an explicit decision before or alongside SFCC-282/796.
- Breakpoint confirmation: commit 6 used `breakpoints.xl` (1280px) where plan prose said "desktop
  ≥1440" — the real Figma frame set has no data point between 834 and 1440, so 1280 is a legitimate,
  disclosed engineering call, not a defect. Still needs a 30-second confirm with design before the
  PR closes, per the original finding.
- **Resolved, not still open:** an earlier note during this build flagged `session-notes.md:395`'s
  "grey info icon" line as a possible stale reference needing a doc correction. It was not stale —
  it was the exact, correct, independently-corroborating citation for the icon commit 8's rework
  added. No doc correction needed; struck from Outstanding.

**Found by step 4.6's Scorer (2026-09-21) — the real, composed cart drawer has never been visually
rendered anywhere, by anyone, correctly scoped as step 9's problem, not this step's.** Real product
rows, real remove/wishlist links, real empty state, real button group, all together for the first
time — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx` isn't mounted anywhere yet (step 9 does that), and its own test
suite correctly mocks every child to a bare stub, per this step's own proportionate scope. Flagged
specifically because step 9 (`_app`/`product-view` wiring) is a **Tier 2 Global Shell** change —
both squads plus tier-2 and tier-1 approvers, a materially heavier-gated PR than a normal step. If
mounting it surfaces a purely visual problem, that fix would land inside the harder-to-review PR
instead of a simple one. **Recommendation: take a quick local dev-server look at the composed
drawer as soon as step 9 mounts it, before that PR goes up for full review** — the nested guest-auth
drawer opening on top of the still-open cart drawer (two stacked Chakra drawer portals) is the one
scenario worth checking first; nothing in this build has visually exercised that combination yet.

**Found by step 4.6's Scorer (2026-09-21) — a meta-observation, not a new finding of its own.**
This is the second time in this build (after the footer decomposition) a step correctly declined to
fix a real duplication because the fix lived in a file outside its own manifest (here:
`CartWishlistAuthGate` vs. `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`'s duplicated responsive-sizing logic). Each
deferral is individually correct and disclosed, but they're scattered across different sections of
this file with no single collected list for a real "go fix these" decision. Worth a standing
follow-up list — grep this file for "DRY" to find them all — rather than each being rediscovered
independently later.

**Found by the final step's Tester (2026-09-21), disclosed candidly by its own Implementer, not
smuggled in — a real but low-stakes `components.md` naming-convention gap, recommended as a
fast-follow, not fixed in this commit.** `useCartDrawer.ts` exports four things from one file
(`CartDrawerContext`, `useCartDrawerState`, `useCartDrawer`, `CartDrawerProvider`) — only one
matches the file's own name, and `components.md`'s "exported function name matches filename" rule
is written for a single-export file. The cited precedent, `useUiCopy.ts`, doesn't fully support
bundling them: it genuinely splits its own Provider into a separate file
(`uiCopyProvider/index.tsx`), which `CartDrawerProvider` didn't get here — deliberately, since
splitting it out would have meant creating a file outside this step's own manifest. Worth a small
follow-up PR (move `CartDrawerProvider` to its own file, matching `useUiCopy`'s own precedent
exactly) once this ships, not a blocker now.

**Found by the final step's Tester (2026-09-21) — a reminder for whoever writes the eventual PR
body, not a new finding.** This exact commit's changed files (`_app/index.tsx`, `product-view.tsx`)
fall outside every existing e2e area allow-list, including the new `cart` group added in commit 1 —
so per `testing.md`'s own change-scoped-E2E rule, this PR gets **zero automated E2E coverage at PR
time**, on the single highest-blast-radius commit in the entire epic (the one that makes the drawer
reachable by a real shopper for the first time). `plan.md` already names this as a "known limit" to
state explicitly in the PR body — flagging here so it doesn't get lost by commit 20 of 20's own
excitement. Make sure it actually lands in the real PR description, not just in this file.

## Not yet fixed, deliberately — a real AC gap, under-flagged until now, needs its own decision

**The quantity stepper does not persist a quantity change to the real basket. Disclosed at the
moment it was found (step 4.6's own commit message, `d3e7ef92`, "Deliberately out of scope"), but
under-weighted in every summary since — including the orchestrating session's own build-complete
report to Marcel, which didn't list it among the open items at all until asked directly whether
everything in the plan actually works end-to-end (2026-09-21).** A shopper can click `+`/`−` on a
cart line right now and the number on screen changes — `ZimmQuantityStepper` (step 3.1) and its
wiring into `product-item` (step 3.5) both work exactly as built and tested. What never happens:
`cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (step 4.6, the only place that renders a real `<ProductItem>`) never
passes an `onItemQuantityChange` prop, so `ProductItem`'s own no-op default (`async () => true`)
is what actually runs — the change is accepted locally and never reaches the server. Checked
directly against the real code before writing this, not assumed.

**This is a real gap against the plan's own stated ACs, not a nice-to-have nobody asked for.**
SFCC-271's own AC text (session-notes.md) describes `+`/`−` incrementing/decrementing "with item
total and order summary updating" — a live, server-reflected change, not a purely local one. No
step anywhere in the 20-commit plan ever claims wiring this — it fell into the same shape of gap
this build found and fixed twice already for other pieces (a component built and tested in
isolation, whose real integration point was described in prose but never turned into an actual
manifest line) — except this one was never caught and inserted as a new step the way the 3.5 and
4.6 insertions were. Needs a decision: insert a 21st commit to wire it now, or accept and log it
as a known post-build gap alongside the others below.

## Not yet fixed, deliberately — needs a product decision, not more engineering

**Found by step 5.1's Tester (2026-09-21) — `checkoutOwner: 'hybrid'` (US) cannot currently be
branched correctly, by any implementation, because the signal it needs doesn't exist yet.**
`countries.ts`'s own doc comment says Global-e should take over "when the user's shipping
destination is outside the site's domestic market" — a per-shopper, shipping-address-based
condition. `useCountryConfig()` is purely static (matches only on site + locale), with no way to
observe an individual shopper's shipping address anywhere in this codebase — confirmed via a
full-repo grep, no country-selector/ship-to mechanism exists (REG-028, the card both integration
docs point to, isn't built). So `ZimmCartButtonGroup` — or any component reading this field today —
structurally cannot satisfy the doc comment's literal claim for a hybrid site; it can only ever
show the same three buttons regardless of where a US shopper is actually shipping. Shipped as

content.content:
show the same three buttons regardless of where a US shopper is actually shipping. Shipped as
always-domestic for `hybrid` (matches `sfcc`), the only currently-answerable reading.
Compounding wrinkle, also found: `.docs/integration/08-global-e.md`'s own checkout matrix still
describes the pre-2026-07-10 single-site US model; `.docs/prd/regional.md` and
`.docs/memory/projectState.md` both say that was superseded by the `ZimmermannUSIntl` site split,
and the code agrees with the two-site version — so it's genuinely unclear whether `hybrid` even
still needs dynamic per-shipment behaviour post-split, or whether `08-global-e.md` is just stale.
**Needs one of two decisions before this ships:** (a) accept always-domestic for `hybrid` as a
documented interim limitation (in both this component and `countries.ts`'s own comment) pending a
real country/ship-to selector, or (b) reconcile the two conflicting docs first, since that
determines whether the gap is even still real. Not blocking this step's own PASS — nothing in this
step's own scope could have built the missing signal.

**Found by step 4.6's Orchestrator (2026-09-21) — confirms and sharpens a risk step 14's own
Scorer explicitly predicted watching for.** Commit 14's Scorer flagged: `queryClient.isMutating()`
is unscoped by mutation key everywhere in this codebase, so it can't distinguish the merge/cap
chain's own write from any unrelated mutation anywhere in the app — "harmless with one caller
wired, worth watching once step 4.6 adds a second one alongside real concurrent traffic." Step 4.6
is that second caller (the wishlist-resume gating effect also reads `queryClient.isMutating()`) —
and turns out to add a *third* source on the same shared client: this same container's own
`removeItemFromBasketMutation`/`createCustomerProductListItem` calls run on the identical
`QueryClient`. A shopper clicking Remove on one line at the exact moment their own wishlist-auth
resume is waiting to fire will see that wait stretch out for a reason unrelated to the merge/cap
chain it's actually watching. Bounded: per the same same-commit-registration reasoning that makes
the wait mechanism itself correct, this can only ever delay, never wrongly skip, the eventual
transition — a rare UX blip, not a correctness bug. Worth a decision: accept as-is, or scope
basket mutations by key at some point (a bigger change, not this build's to make unprompted).

**Found by step 4.6's Tester (2026-09-21), live-rendered not assumed — a real, pre-existing
`/product/undefined` broken link, reachable today via base's own `/cart` route, not introduced by
this build.** `item-name.tsx` derives its link `href` from `variant?.master?.masterId ||
variant.id` — never `variant.productId`. For any basket line whose catalog product has since been
discontinued/deleted (a normal occurrence for a seasonal fashion retailer), there's no fetched
product record and no `id` field on a raw basket line, so the rendered link resolves to
`/product/undefined`. Confirmed this is not new: base's own `product-item-list/index.jsx` builds
the identical merge shape and would hit the same gap. `cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (step 4.6) reaches
this pre-existing gap through a second, parallel path, it doesn't create it. Root cause lives in
`item-name.tsx`, outside every step's manifest in this build — needs its own ticket, not a fix here.

**Found by step 4.6's Tester (2026-09-21) — a citation-provenance question, needs Marcel's own
Jira check, not resolvable from this session (no Jira tool available here).** "AC10" is cited as
settled fact in 4 places across this codebase (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`
×2, `zimmDrawer/index.tsx` ×2) for the "focus returns to the trigger on close" requirement — but a
full-text search of every SFCC-11 build artifact (`plan.md`, `handoff.md`, `findings.md`) found
**zero** matches for "AC10" anywhere; only "AC7" exists, for a related-but-distinct assertion (the
top-level drawer's own `finalFocusRef`, not this specific nested case). Either a real Jira AC
(`customfield_10231`) that these build docs simply never captured, or a citation that drifted in
at some point and has been propagated code-comment-to-code-comment across 4 files ever since with
nobody checking it against the source. Worth a direct look at the real ticket before this ships.

**Found by step 4.6's Tester (2026-09-21) — the AC10 focus-return degradation comment in
`cartDrawerContainer.tsx` was factually wrong about what actually happens, found and corrected in
this same step.** It claimed the fallback lands on `document.body`; live-rendering the real close
sequence showed focus actually lands on the outer, still-open cart drawer's own `aria-hidden`
initial-focus sentinel instead — a real UX gap (a keyboard user parked on an invisible, unannounced
element), not the previously-claimed behaviour. Comment corrected to describe the real mechanism;
the underlying UX gap itself is not fixed and needs its own follow-up ticket.

**Found by step 4.6's Tester (2026-09-21) — a systemic, pre-existing story-coverage gap this step
continues, not a fresh gap it introduces.** No `.stories.tsx` exists for `cartDrawerContainer.tsx`.
Checked against `components.md`'s actual text (no carve-out for `overrides/app/pages/`) and against
precedent in this exact codebase (`checkout/partials/payment.stories.tsx` already successfully
mocks live SDK hooks in a story) — neither justifies skipping one. Broadened the check: **10 of 18
non-test `.tsx` files under `overrides/app/pages/` have no story at all**, including the three
other heaviest SDK-hook-owning containers (`product-detail`, `home`, `product-list`). Not this
step's own gap to fix in isolation — worth its own scope decision (retrofit stories on the heavy
containers, or amend `components.md` with an explicit, honest carve-out for page-level containers
that own live commerce-SDK state) rather than each future page quietly repeating the same gap.

**Found by step 4.6's Tester (2026-09-21), correctly left alone — a DRY finding whose own
justification no longer holds, but fixing it means touching a file outside every current step's
manifest.** `CartWishlistAuthGate` (new, this step) duplicates `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`'s
responsive drawer-sizing logic, on the reasoning that the original governs two breakpoints. Checked
directly: `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`'s own `isTabletOrAbove` value is dead for rendering purposes (its
`drawerSize` ternary only reads `isDesktopOrAbove`), so both files' actually-executed logic is
identical today — the "two breakpoints" justification doesn't hold, but extracting a shared hook
would require modifying `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` itself (Hard Rule 5, not this step's
file). Worth a follow-up ticket, not a blocker.

**Found by step 5.1's Scorer (2026-09-21), pulled from this build's own pre-build Figma audit
(`figma-reference/international-storefront.md`, written 2026-09-19, predating this step) — a real,
currently-unowned Figma element sits right below the button group.** A "Duties and taxes are
included in the price displayed" disclosure line, positioned between the button group and the
promotion-code accordion. Correctly NOT built by this step — it's architecturally a drawer/
organism-level element (the button-group molecule's job stops at the buttons), and per §11.6's own
content list, the promotion-code accordion beneath it is separately owned by SFCC-191 (Squad B,
Bianca) and the whole "Totals summary" column it sits inside is already out of this epic's scope
(SFCC-816/274 — see the cart sale-pricing-gaps memory and this file's own step 4.6 notes on the
RHS column). Most likely this disclosure line belongs to that same deferred SFCC-816 scope, not a
new fourth thing — but nobody has explicitly assigned it anywhere, so it's flagged here rather than
assumed folded in silently. The same audit also flags a **mobile-breakpoint Checkout button** in
Figma sized `h40/px20` against the uniform `h52/px32` this build ships everywhere — the audit
itself calls this "possibly a Figma-file inconsistency, not resolved," and plan.md's own explicit
uniform-sizing spec implicitly supersedes it; a defensible call, not treated as a defect, but worth
a 30-second design confirm before the PR closes, same treatment as the existing 1280-vs-1440
breakpoint item already logged below.

**Found by step 5.1's Tester (2026-09-21) — the base, unstyled `/cart` page is still fully live,
with no redirect into the new drawer.** `pages/cart/index.jsx` + `cart-cta.jsx` still work exactly
as before, still call `useCurrentBasket()` and can mutate the real basket — plan.md's own model
calls `/cart` "dead" only in the sense that nothing *in-app* links to it anymore (confirmed: no
step in the 20-commit manifest, including the final trigger-wiring commit, actually intercepts a
direct `/cart` navigation). A bookmarked link, a typed URL, or an old external link still lands a
shopper on a fully functional but completely unstyled alternate checkout surface that received
none of this epic's work. Needs a decision before the PR closes: accept as a known interim gap (the
in-app experience is fully replaced, only a direct-URL edge case is exposed), or add an actual
redirect as part of commit 20's own scope.

## Not yet fixed, deliberately

`overrides/app/components/icons/` and `item-variant/`'s CODEOWNERS gaps — real, named, not this
build skill's to fix (CODEOWNERS is Tier 1 Governance). Carry into the PR body per AGENTS.md's own
"When to Stop and Ask a Human" table, and raise as one combined CODEOWNERS PR afterward rather than
three separate ones.

**Found by step 3.6's Tester (2026-09-19), not this step's to fix — 2 of `ZimmButton`'s 7 real
`variant="icon"` consumers have no component-level test file at all**: `zimmInputAction`
(→ `zimmSubscribeSection`) and `zimmDrawer` (→ `zimmCartDrawer`/`zimmPdpDrawer`/
`zimmWishlistAuthDrawer`/`product-detail`, 5 consumers) — only Storybook `play` coverage, which
never asserts on any `aria-*` attribute. Pre-existing, not introduced by this step, but newly
relevant: this step just gave the icon variant a new, silently-droppable `ariaDescribedBy` prop
with zero regression protection in either consumer. Creating either test file would mean touching
files outside this step's own manifest — the same shape of question the `zimmButton.tsx` extension
already was — so flagged for a decision rather than done unilaterally. Worth a follow-up ticket if
not picked up sooner.

**Found the same pass — a real gap in what "Storybook a11y check green" has ever actually proven,
worth Marcel seeing directly, not just filed away**: axe-core's `target-size` rule (WCAG 2.2 AA SC
2.5.8 — the exact rule underpinning this epic's own "ship the 24px touch target, don't escalate"
decision on the stepper, session-notes.md §11.8) produced **zero results across all 320 Storybook
a11y tests**, meaning it isn't firing at all in this repo's `@storybook/addon-a11y` configuration.

## SFCC-11 Cart bundle — AC coverage audit (read-only)

**Headline: the HANDOFF is stale.** It was written at commit 20 (`17ceffcc`, 2026-09-21); the branch now carries **72 commits**. Its one flagged "real AC gap" (stepper not persisting to basket) was closed on 2026-09-22 by `e3694c7a`. Verdicts below are against **code**, not the HANDOFF.

### 1. Genuinely not delivered / contradicts a recorded decision

| # | Item | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Stepper touch target is 12px, not the 24px that was decided.** session-notes §11.11(1) settles this explicitly ("BUILD 24px", justified 3 ways incl. WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8, AGENTS.md's stated standard). Commit `1ee87ab1` (2026-09-23, Marcel-authored) overrides `ZimmButton`'s icon size down to `--zimm-scale-s` (12px) via `sx`, root gap 8px→12px. | `.../molecules/zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx:116,131` + `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts` |
| | **Cannot tell from the artefacts whether this was re-decided.** The commit body asserts "deliberate, informed WCAG 2.5.8 override" but no artefact records the reversal — the decision record still says the opposite. Needs your confirmation, not mine. | |
| **2** | **`checkoutOwner: 'hybrid'` (US) ships always-domestic — HANDOFF says this "needs one of two decisions **before this ships**"; no decision is recorded anywhere.** Not an engineering gap (the ship-to signal doesn't exist, REG-028 unbuilt), but the required decision is outstanding. | `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx:193` (`isInternational = checkoutOwner === 'global-e'`) |
| **3** | **Base `/cart` remains fully live with no redirect into the drawer.** HANDOFF: "needs a decision before the PR closes" — none recorded. Direct-URL/bookmark lands on an unstyled parallel surface. | no interception in any of the 72 commits |
| **4** | **"AC10" (focus-return) is cited as settled in 4 files but appears in zero artefacts.** Unresolvable without Jira. | `cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`×2, `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`×2 |

### 2. Per-story verdicts

**SFCC-315 (9 ACs) — all DELIVERED.** Header `BAG • {n}` / `YOUR BAG IS EMPTY` (`zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx:119`); count live off basket cache; right-side panel + overlay, mobile full-width (`zimmDrawer.css.ts:144`); X/overlay/Escape close + `finalFocusRef` restore (`zimmDrawer/index.tsx:305`); scroll preserved via `body.overflow` lock, not `position:fixed` (`:286–293`). Empty **body** correctly SFCC-277's.

**SFCC-270 (9 ACs) — all DELIVERED.** 8-file override (`product-item/` + `item-variant/`) per the Option-B decision; colour+size as one string via `combineAttributeValues` (`item-attributes.tsx:149`) satisfies the two separate ACs; stepper with `+`/`−` either side; Remove/Wishlist underlined below (`ZimmCartItemActions`); `item-name` spread-order fix made.

**SFCC-271 (4 ACs) — all DELIVERED.** `onItemQuantityChange` → real `updateItemInBasket` (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:361,693`); `−` inert at min, resolves `false` on rejection; bag badge uncapped total quantity (`c22fcf3c`, `e483c152`).

**SFCC-795 —** default/stepper/warning states, responsive, and the 11 a11y ACs **DELIVERED** (`9183524b` sweep; `aria-live`, `ariaDescribedBy` pairing). Was/now price **DELIVERED** via `DisplayPrice` (`item-price.tsx`, per-unit fix `98b0d609`). **Error states (OOS/Partial/Unavailable): DEFERRED-BY-DECISION** — presentation built and storied, triggering owned by SFCC-282/796 (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx:317`). **Discount label: DEFERRED-BY-DECISION** — built as `ZimmInlineMessage variant="success"`, deliberately unwired pending the promotions engine. **44×44 AC: DEVIATION-BY-DECISION** (see gap 1 — now 12px, not even the 24px that was substituted).

**SFCC-272 (8 ACs) — 8/8 addressed.** Remove, last-item empty state (`ZimmCartEmptyState`, `:769`), full-line removal, wishlist move + guest gate (`CartWishlistAuthGate`) + cross-auth resume (`usePendingWishlistItem`, per-`productId` namespaced) all DELIVERED. **Banner *surface* DEFERRED-BY-DECISION to SFCC-404** — copy/behaviour shipped via `useCartMessages` toasts (`defineMessages`, single handler).

**SFCC-250 (9 ACs).** AC1/2/5/6/7 DELIVERED (`useCartMergeAndCap`, `sum_quantities` + `claimBasketMerge` now on **both** sign-in surfaces — `use-auth-modal.tsx:188`, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:205` — plus `>=` per-line cap, loop guard, live `queryClient.isMutating()`). AC3/8 DEFERRED-BY-DECISION (SFCC-404). AC4/9 nothing-to-build by decision. **BM value UNVERIFIABLE as stated** — `getMaxOrderQuantity` reads `c_maxOrderQuantity`, falls back to 3 (`utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts:51`); SFCC-268 undeployed.

**SFCC-275 (8 ACs).** AC1/2/8 DELIVERED (three buttons, fixed order, express *removed* not hidden). AC3/4 DELIVERED-AS-SCOPED (buttons always enabled; backend blocking deliberately out of a UI story). AC5 DELIVERED. AC6/7 branch built, destination stubbed BY DECISION (`navigateInternationalCheckoutStub`) — but see gap 2.

**Recommendations rail + promo code: OUT-OF-SCOPE-BY-DECISION**, correctly absent.

Audit complete — report delivered.

**Key finding:** the HANDOFF is stale (written at commit 20 of what is now 72), so its own flagged "real AC gap" — the quantity stepper not persisting to the basket — was actually closed the next day by `e3694c7a`. All verdicts were taken against the code, not the build record.

**Genuinely not delivered (4 items, ranked):**
1. The quantity stepper's touch target is **12px**, while session-notes §11.11(1) explicitly settled on **24px** (WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8, AGENTS.md's stated standard). Commit `1ee87ab1` overrode it down via `sx`. The commit body claims it was deliberate; no artefact records the reversal — flagged as un-adjudicable rather than guessed.
2. `checkoutOwner: 'hybrid'` (US) ships always-domestic; HANDOFF says this needs a decision *before shipping* and none is recorded.
3. Base `/cart` still fully live with no redirect into the drawer — same shape, decision never made.
4. "AC10" cited as settled fact in 4 files, zero matches in any artefact.

Everything else resolves to DELIVERED or to a deliberate deferral (SFCC-404 banners, SFCC-282/796 error triggering, the unwired discount label, SFCC-277's empty body) — reported as decisions, not gaps.
